newsitem.title: FINLAND: FAST FALL IN FINNISH JOBLESS MAY UP INFLATION - VATT.
newsitem.headline: FAST FALL IN FINNISH JOBLESS MAY UP INFLATION - VATT.

text.p: The fall in unemployment may accelerate but a rapid decline could boost inflation since structural unemployment is high, the Government Institute of Economic Research (VATT) said on Thursday.
It estimated structural unemployment at around 300,000 with the so-called NAIRU method which it said measures the unemployment level below which inflation would speed up.

"No significant inflationary pressures are in sight at the moment. However, with structural unemployment as high as it is, a fast decline in joblessness could make inflation accelerate," the government think-tank said.
"Economic growth is currently clearly strengthening, and if recent forecasts materialise, unemployment may now ease significantly faster than before," it said.
In March, there were 424,100 unemployed and the jobless rate was 17.3 percent according to the labour ministry, and Statistics Finland estimated February unemployment at 394,00 or 15.8 percent.
